history.summary: Sri Anantheswara Temple is an old Shiva temple in Anantapur city, Andhra Pradesh. A single travel article lists it alongside the Sri Anjaneya Swamy Temple as one of the two most important temples in the city, both on the banks of the Penna (Pennar) river; no published history, building date, or patron dynasty was found (flag: uncertain identity, weak sourcing). Note: it is unrelated to the famous Anantheshwara Temple at Udupi, Karnataka, which dominates web searches for this name. Coordinates are approximate (geocoded city temple POI, not a verified Anantheswara Temple match).

town_description: Anantapur (Anantapuramu) is a city in the Rayalaseema region of Andhra Pradesh and headquarters of Anantapur district. Founded in the Vijayanagara period and named after the Anantasagara tank, it is a pilgrimage town with numerous temples and a staging point for Lepakshi, Penukonda, Gooty Fort and Puttaparthi.

travel.airport: Kempegowda International Airport, Bengaluru (~200 km); taxi or bus to Anantapur, then auto-rickshaw within the city
travel.railway: Anantapur Railway Station (ATP) on the Hyderabad-Bengaluru line
travel.road: On National Highway 44 (Hyderabad-Bengaluru); APSRTC and private buses connect to Hyderabad, Bengaluru, Chennai and Tirupati

visitor_information.best_time: October to February (cool season; summers are very hot)
